metric.definition: Liters of water consumed by the facility, chiefly for evaporative cooling, per kilowatt-hour of IT energy delivered.

reading.body:
WUE, Water Usage Effectiveness, measures liters of water consumed by a facility, chiefly for evaporative cooling, per kilowatt-hour of IT energy delivered, calculated as annual site water use in liters divided by IT energy in kilowatt-hours.

Water is named as the constraint communities notice first, and the site makes an important point about the relationship between this metric and PUE, evaporative cooling trades electricity for water, so a facility can report a low, efficient PUE while hiding a high WUE, and permitting fights increasingly turn on this specific number rather than the more commonly reported power efficiency figure. Operators using little or no evaporative cooling report WUE near zero, while water-cooled designs in hot climates run substantially higher, according to the source.

It sits alongside Carbon Usage Effectiveness and renewable energy utilization under Sustainability, and The Green Grid is named as the source body defining the metric.
